levels.0: Lists 'post and read feed' with no ranking, freshness or deletion requirements.
levels.1: Covers posting, a ranked feed and following, but not deletes, blocks or what the author sees after posting.
levels.2: Posting, ranked feed with scroll, follow/unfollow, deletes, blocks and mutes; eventual consistency for followers with read-your-own-writes for the author; recommendations and ads explicitly out of scope.

levels.1: States 300 ms and 'real time' without separating read availability from freshness.
levels.2: 300 ms p99 for page one, one-minute freshness as the contract, feed reads more available than posting, and a stale feed accepted over an empty one.

levels.0: No numbers, or numbers without derivation.
levels.1: Derives feed reads and posts per second but not the fan-out rate or the celebrity cost.
levels.2: 52k pages/s average and 156k at peak; 3.5k posts/s and 10.4k at peak; 140 inserts per post → 1.46M inserts/s at peak; one 50M-follower post = 35M inserts ≈ 23 s of spare capacity.

levels.1: Sizes the feed cache by memory only, or the API fleet with no headroom for a zone.
levels.2: 300 IDs × ~20 B ≈ 6 KB per user → 2.4 TB; timeline cluster sized by inserts (60 primaries); post store by bytes (48 nodes); API fleet sized for ρ ≤ 0.55 with a zone lost because latency, not throughput, sets it.

levels.1: GET feed and POST post with bodies, but page-number pagination or no idempotency.
levels.2: Cursor-based GET /v1/feed with an opaque cursor and a new-posts count, POST /v1/posts with an Idempotency-Key, and presigned uploads so image bytes bypass the API.

levels.0: One SQL table of posts joined against follows at read time.
levels.1: Separate posts, follows and a feed cache, but feeds hold full posts or store choices are unexplained.
levels.2: Snowflake post IDs, feeds of IDs only, author_posts for recent-by-author, follows in both directions sharded by user, feed sessions; wide-column posts and sharded MySQL graph justified by access pattern; feed cache treated as rebuildable.

levels.1: Walks posting and reading but fan-out is a box with no detail.
levels.2: Post write then event; workers page followers, skip inactive and celebrity authors, insert IDs and trim; read merges timeline + celebrity posts, filters, ranks with a timeout, stores a session, hydrates; latency budget per step.

levels.0: Picks push or pull without considering the 50M-follower account.
levels.1: Proposes a hybrid but with an arbitrary threshold and no plan for the pull side's cost.
levels.2: Quantifies both extremes, derives the threshold from spare fan-out capacity and freshness (≤ ~2M, pick 1M with hysteresis), keeps celebrity posts in memory on API instances, skips inactive followers, does not fan out deletes.

levels.1: Sorted set of IDs with a cap, but no answer for users without a cached feed.
levels.2: Capped sorted set with compact encoding traded against insert cost, sizing per primary, a rebuild path from following + recent-by-author lists, and the lost-shard case rate-limited with a fallback page.

criteria.title: Ranking in budget and cursor pagination

levels.0: Ranking ignored or unbounded; offset pagination.
levels.1: Ranks with a model but no timeout or fallback; timestamp cursors applied to a ranked feed.
levels.2: Two-stage candidates → light model with precomputed features, 80 ms timeout with chronological fallback and breaker; feed-session cursor for ranked pages with chronological continuation and a sized session store.

criteria.title: Failure modes and the fan-out backlog

levels.1: Lists cache and zone failures but not fan-out lag.
levels.2: Covers lag, shard loss, ranker outage, cache loss, zone loss, Kafka outage and deletes; gives a live-event timeline with detection, the threshold lever and computed drain time.

levels.1: Scales components linearly without naming what breaks first.
levels.2: Names fan-out writes as the first break (~600 primaries) with ordered levers, memory and ranking costs, per-region fan-out; each key decision stated with its alternative and the reason.
